chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idrees, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan, from Amr ibn Saeed, from Musaddaq ibn Sadqa, from Ammar ibn Musa, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about the one in Ihram picking (cleaning) his teeth; he said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمِ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible
key_terms.يَتَخَلَّلُ: Picking or cleaning the teeth (often with a miswak)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to clean their teeth?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that a pilgrim in Ihram may use a miswak for oral hygiene, resolving potential concerns about minor actions disrupting the sacred state. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential principle of ease (yusr) in ritual purity, distinguishing between acts that nullify Ihram and those that merely maintain cleanliness. The ruling underscores the balance between spiritual devotion and physical well-being during Hajj and Umrah.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, and Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Hassan, from Amro Bin Saeed, from Musaddaq Bin Sadawa, from Ammar Bin Musa, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the one in Ihraam, whether he can pick (clean) his teeth’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya and Ahmad ibn Idris has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn al-Hassan from ’Amr ibn Sa‘id from Musaddiq ibn Sadaqah from ‘Ammar ibn Musa who has said the following:
“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who uses a toothpick while he is in the state of Ihram. He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not harmful.’”
